clue.text: Trotter's back, admitting work was not on the level

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece is taken inside the other
back tells us the name with its possessive is read from end to start

parts.note: Del Boy Trotter of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, so Trotter's is DEL'S
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone notes a Trotter was idle on the job and not honest about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the name and its possessive end to start, giving SLED, and 'admitting' takes the work inside. Del Boy Trotter is the wheeler-dealer hero of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that slopes is tilted, so it is not level.

clue.text: Windows removed after this order, at the end of the day?

definitions.text: order, at the end of the day?

parts.note: lights is an old word for windows, as in leaded lights
something removed has been taken away, so it is out

explanation.surface: Blackout curtains come down once this command is given at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after this' joins the wordplay to the definition, the bedtime command in a dormitory or barracks to switch the lamps off.
explanation.definitionFit: The call given at bedtime in a school or barracks to switch every lamp off.

clue.text: Randy old ruler briefly caught on film

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend
a pic is a picture, a film

explanation.surface: A lustful old monarch is snapped by a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final M of PRIAM, king of Troy, to give PRIA; 'caught on' just joins it to PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lustful, which the adjective drawn from the phallic god Priapus describes.

clue.text: Away from public attention, guide leader is into good works

indicators.note: is into means goes inside, so one piece is placed within the other
works here is a verb meaning reshapes or kneads, so the word before it is rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide leader quietly involves herself in charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges GOOD to DOGO, and 'is into' puts G, the first letter of 'guide', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is a British idiom for staying hidden and keeping quiet.

clue.text: I'm a fool to take charge of criminal investigation

parts.note: to head something is to lead it
a police case is an inquiry into a crime

explanation.surface: A detective admits being a dunce to be leading the inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcase is British slang for a crazy or foolish person, and the clue speaks as that person.

clue.text: Enjoying oneself putting on a military display

explanation.surface: Having fun while staging a parade of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a field day is an idiom for great fun, and a field day was originally a day of troop exercises and review.

clue.text: Rand invested in new African-English travel company

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
new signals the following word is to be made afresh in another order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: South African money is put into a new Anglo-African tourism business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AFRICAN to AIFRANC, 'invested in' puts R into it, and E for English goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The national airline of France flies passengers, so it is a carrier in the travel trade.

clue.text: Man at last has raised pounds for clothes

indicators.note: has means holds, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate or fellow
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man finally collects money to buy something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' puts L inside COBBER; 'at last' and 'raised' only colour the surface. Clobber is British and Australian slang for clothes and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is slang for one's garments and kit.

clue.text: Labourer, one kept in line

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker and a colleague are kept in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter in many typefaces.

clue.text: Showing great enthusiasm when taking the plunge

explanation.surface: An eager swimmer leaps from a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Going too far with zeal is an idiom from literally falling from a ship into the sea.

clue.text: Resign, now dept's reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged differently, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official quits because the department has been restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganised' rearranges NOW and DEPTS (the apostrophe gives no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a post voluntarily is to quit it, an idiom also used of officials.

clue.text: Snub a specialist in religious education

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a buff is an enthusiast who knows a field well

explanation.surface: Cold-shoulder an expert in RE teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the name of the school subject Religious Education in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a curt refusal or brush-off.

clue.text: No doubt soldiers — reservists — will follow regimental leader home

indicators.note: will follow means the reservists come after the leader's letter

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
in means at home

explanation.surface: Troops and reservists will certainly follow their colonel back to barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force; 'will follow' sets TA after R, the first letter of 'regimental'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean surely, without question.

clue.text: Checked 19 again, as told

explanation.surface: Someone recalculated the figures as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is NUMBERS, so the first sense is going over the figures a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To count figures again and to narrate a story share one spelling.

clue.text: TV presenter's crude introduction is cut

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, and cut means it is removed

parts.note: gross means vulgar or crude

explanation.surface: A television host's vulgar opener is edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a long-serving British TV and radio presenter; 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Ross is a well-known British broadcaster and chat-show host.

clue.text: One stops being more resolute

explanation.surface: Someone who halts is more determined.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stanches a flow halts it, and staunch also means steadfast, giving a comparative.

clue.text: Sailor on street getting shot

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the sailor comes after the street

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in the street gets shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab is having a try, as is having a shot.

clue.text: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed

definitions.text: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed

parts.words: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed
parts.note: a fire or rocket stage that has used all its fuel stops and must be relit, as a worn-out worker must begin afresh

explanation.surface: An overworked person is told they need a fresh beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Total fatigue from overwork is named after a fire that has used up its fuel.

clue.text: Conflict, an atrocity to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Conflict, an atrocity to (7,3)', is cut short: CRIME (atrocity) + AN accounts for CRIMEAN, but no word gives WAR; no scan and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Songs from the sixties, perhaps

explanation.surface: Pop tunes of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical items in a show are called numbers, and 60 to 69 are examples of figures.

clue.text: Glimpse what's stuck in paper cups

indicators.note: stuck in says the letters are lodged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A look at something lodged in disposable cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' points to the letters inside 'paper cups'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a quick insight or brief look at something.

clue.text: Do down

parts.note: read as an instruction to groom one's feathers, as a bird does to its soft plumage

explanation.surface: Belittle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do down' normally means belittle; here 'do' means groom and 'down' is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird tidying its plumage with its beak grooms its feathers.

clue.text: Dressing to secure injured tissue

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: lint is a fabric used for dressing wounds
a game leg is an injured or lame one

explanation.surface: A bandage is used to hold damaged tissue in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like part of a salad or a costume, but it is a wound covering; 'to secure' wraps it round the second piece. 'Game' meaning lame is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of fibrous tissue joining bones.

clue.text: Cigarette smoking initially banned: one looks surprised

indicators.note: banned means excluded, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: gasper is old British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word smoking

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that smoking has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks S from 'smoking', and 'banned' removes it from GASPER, old British slang for a cheap cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is someone who stares open-mouthed in surprise.

clue.text: Distorted version of prophet's decree, not the actual words

indicators.note: a distorted version jumbles the original, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone twisted what the prophet decreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distorted version of' rearranges PROPHETS and DECREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect quotation gives the sense of what someone said rather than the words they used.

clue.text: Tune idly composed in harmonious style

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A melody written lazily but sweetly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together as one is acting in harmony.

clue.text: Rearrange where to go on holiday

explanation.surface: Change the plans for a vacation spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is re-sort, to sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort again is to rearrange, and a holiday destination is a seaside or ski town.
